rationale:
Issue #2591 states that NonBlockingFileIO.read(...) should error when more than 4 GiB is requested instead of silently returning less. The pre-fix code in Sources/NIOPosix/NonBlockingFileIO.swift clamped the request (`let byteCount = rawByteCount < Int32.max ? rawByteCount : size_t(Int32.max)`) in both read0 overloads, returning a short ByteBuffer with neither an error nor end-of-file, which contradicts the documented short-read-only-at-EOF contract. The minimized patch keeps exactly the two hunks that replace that clamp with `guard byteCount <= UInt32.max` returning/throwing IOError(EINVAL) in the EventLoopFuture and async read0; the `rawByteCount` -> `byteCount` parameter rename is mechanically required by removing the clamped local, and the added comments document the new guard. No formatting-only, config-only, doc-only, feature, or test changes remain in the production patch (single file, single symbol pair). The triggers come from the fixing commit itself and exercise only pre-existing public API (`read(fileHandle:byteCount:allocator:eventLoop:)` and its async overload) plus the pre-existing IOError/EINVAL types, asserting the exact reported symptom (a byteCount of Int(UInt32.max) &+ 1 must fail); no API introduced by the fix is used. Strict machine evidence reports build.both_versions PASS, selectors present/unique (2), trigger.buggy_differential reproducing both selectors, trigger.fixed_clean PASS, trigger.deterministic 4/4 fingerprint groups over 3 repetitions, and full_suite.fixed_all_green PASS both before and after minimization (post_minimization_validation PASS). active_same_project_root_causes is empty and apple/swift-nio#2591 is in allowed_root_cause_ids, so the root cause is not a registry duplicate.

Issue #2591 ("NonBlockingFileIO.read(...) don't error if more than 4 GiB is requested") states that a ByteBuffer cannot hold more than 4 GiB and that read must error rather than silently satisfy an impossible request. The buggy revision clamps with `let byteCount = rawByteCount < Int32.max ? rawByteCount : size_t(Int32.max)` in both read0 overloads, returning a short buffer with no error and no EOF. The minimized production patch retains exactly the two hunks that replace that clamp with `guard byteCount <= UInt32.max else { ... IOError(errnoCode: EINVAL, ...) }` in the EventLoopFuture and async read0, plus the mechanically required parameter rename from `byteCount rawByteCount` to `byteCount` that the removed clamp line made necessary. Both hunks are in one production file (Sources/NIOPosix/NonBlockingFileIO.swift); there is no refactor, formatting, docs, config, or test content in the minimized production patch. The trigger comes from the same fixing commit and calls only pre-existing public overloads read(fileHandle:byteCount:allocator:eventLoop:) and the async read, asserting a thrown IOError with errnoCode EINVAL for byteCount Int(UInt32.max) &+ 1 against a small temporary file, with XCTSkipIf for 32-bit platforms; IOError and errnoCode predate the fix, so no new production API is required. The build-compatibility patch only qualifies three FileType annotations as NIOFS.FileType in an integration test and is applied identically to both revisions. Machine evidence gates pass on both the original and post-minimization runs: build.both_versions, selectors.present_and_unique (2 unique), trigger.buggy_differential reproducing both selectors, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (4 fingerprint groups), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green across 38 matrix runs and 3 repetitions. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and apple/swift-nio#2591 is the supplied allowed root cause id.

risks: Minimization dropped the readSync per-syscall cap (hunks 2-3), so requests between Int32.max and UInt32.max now pass a size larger than Int32.max to a single read/pread on the buggy-fixed pair; the benchmark fix therefore covers only the error-path half of the upstream change and the 2-4 GiB full-read behavior is neither restored nor covered by the triggers.

The differential signal is 'throws IOError(EINVAL)' vs 'does not throw'. On the buggy revision the clamp still allocates roughly 2 GiB before returning a short buffer, so the trigger is memory-sensitive in constrained environments even though the recorded matrix was deterministic.
issue_evidence and semantic_justification are null in the case record; issue text was read through source_candidate.issue_check rather than an independently captured issue snapshot.

Full-suite green on the fixed revision depends on one baseline exclusion (Tests/NIOFSIntegrationTests/FileSystemTests.swift::testHomeDirectoryFromPasswd) and on the build-compatibility patch qualifying NIOFS.FileType in integration tests; both are environment scaffolding applied to both revisions, not production behavior.
